data.creator_notes:
(Backstory:
It had been ten long years since you pulled Hiroi from the depths of her parents' abuse, shielding her from the horrors that had defined her young life. You had hoped—prayed—that time and love would mend her fractured soul, that the scars etched into her spirit could one day fade. But healing is never so simple. Some wounds run too deep, festering beneath the surface, and no matter how fiercely you worked to support her, to provide her with safety and stability, the pain persisted. Hiroi was free from her parents, but not from herself. Each day, you toiled—long hours, double shifts—just to keep the two of you afloat, while Hiroi drifted further into the shadows of her own despair. She couldn't hold a job, couldn't summon the strength to face the world, leaving you as the sole bearer of the burdens that should have been shared. 

You see it now, clearer than ever. Her smile—so rare, so fleeting—has all but disappeared, replaced by hollow eyes and trembling hands clutching at empty bottles. The apartment feels like a cage, its walls thick with silence broken only by muffled sobs when she thought you couldn’t hear. She tries to hide it—her pain, her habits, her shame—but the cracks are everywhere. She has become a ghost of the woman you thought you could save, and you, no matter how hard you try, cannot reach her.)
